# P13 — Ruth 4:13-17

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** Obed: the conception YHWH gives, the women's blessing, the child on Naomi's lap
- **BCV:** Ruth 4:13-17
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** HISTORICAL_NARRATIVE
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
Pericope-level INFORMAL_CASUAL — the narrator's telling of the marriage, the birth, and the naming. Scene 2, the women's words to Naomi (4:14–15), lifts to CEREMONIAL: a set "blessed be YHWH" benediction invoking the divine name. Scene 3, Naomi taking the child and the neighbor-women naming him (4:16–17), stays in the pericope-level INFORMAL_CASUAL.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
Boaz takes Ruth, and she becomes his wife, and he comes to her; and YHWH gives her conception, and she bears a son. The women say to Naomi: blessed be YHWH, who has not left you without a redeemer today; may his name be called out in Israel. He will be a restorer of your life and a sustainer of your old age — for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him. Naomi takes the child, sets him on her bosom, and becomes his nurse. And the neighbor-women call out a name for him, saying: a son has been born to Naomi; and they call his name Obed. The narrator adds: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David. What weighs on the passage is where its words fall: the narrator says it is YHWH who gives her conception; the women speak to Naomi, not to Ruth or to Boaz; they call Ruth "your daughter-in-law who loves you"; the neighbor-women say the son is born to Naomi; and the passage ends on three names — Obed, Jesse, David.

### 2.2 Context
At her return Naomi said she went out full and YHWH brought her back empty (1:21); here the women say he will be "a restorer of your life" — in Hebrew "one who brings back", the same verb Naomi used when she said YHWH had brought her back. At her return the women of the town said "Is this Naomi?" (1:19), and Naomi told them: do not call me Naomi, call me Mara (1:20); here the women speak to Naomi, and the neighbor-women call a name — the child's. The word redeemer, heard at 2:20, 3:9, 3:12–13 and at the gate (4:1–8), is spoken again by the women: YHWH has not left Naomi without a redeemer today. At 4:11 all the people at the gate and the elders blessed Boaz and said: call out a name in Bethlehem; here the women bless YHWH and wish: may his name be called out in Israel — the same words, name and call. YHWH's name, spoken in the blessing at the gate, is spoken again in the women's words. At 4:16 the child is "the child" (yeled), the word used at 1:5 for Naomi's two children. The women do not call Ruth by her name or "the Moabite"; she is "your daughter-in-law who loves you", better to Naomi than seven sons. And the last line is the narrator's: Obed is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
Swift, then warm, then still. The opening verse moves fast — take, become, come, give, bear — the agents shifting in a breath, Boaz to YHWH to Ruth, all in one line. The women's blessing opens the passage wide and warm: redeemer, restorer, sustainer, a daughter-in-law better than seven sons. Then it slows to its tenderest image — an old woman with a child against her chest. And the naming closes it quietly: a son for Naomi, his name Obed — and then, in the narrator's own later voice, the names Jesse and David. The mood is warm and settled, and the passage ends on names.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage tells, in one verse, that Boaz takes Ruth, she becomes his wife, he comes to her, YHWH gives her conception, and she bears a son. It gives the women's words to Naomi: blessed be YHWH, who has not left her without a redeemer today; may his name be called out in Israel; he will be a restorer of her life and a sustainer of her old age, for her daughter-in-law, who loves her, who is better to her than seven sons, has borne him. It tells that Naomi takes the child to her bosom and becomes his nurse, and that the neighbor-women call a name for him — a son has been born to Naomi — and call him Obed. And it ends in the narrator's own voice: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David. To speak this passage is to keep the swiftness of the first verse, the warmth of the women's words, the tenderness of the lap, the neighbor-women's "a son has been born to Naomi", and the closing names.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — The marriage, the conception, the birth (4:13)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one who takes Ruth as wife and comes to her; after this verse he is not mentioned again in this passage
- Relationship: now her husband
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — רוּת / Ruth
- Role: the one taken as wife, given conception, who bears a son
- Relationship: the Moabite widow of Mahlon, now Boaz's wife and a mother
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B10-YHWH]] — יְהוָה / YHWH
- Role: the one who gives her conception
- Relationship: the God named throughout the story; here the narrator says he gives her conception
- Presence: REFERENCED

The child — בֵּן / "a son"
- Role: the son born; not yet named
- Relationship: the son Ruth bears after Boaz comes to her
- Presence: PRESENT

**3B — Places**

- None: the text names no place in this verse.

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

- None: no object or concept is named in this verse.

**3D — Times**
- None: no distinct temporal frame; the marriage, the conception, and the birth run as one swift sequence.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B13-Boaz]] Boaz takes [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth, and she becomes his wife, and he comes to her; and [[B10-YHWH]] YHWH gives her conception, and she bears a son.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Tells the marriage and the birth in a single swift line, with YHWH's giving of conception at its center.

**Significant Absence**
The narrator tells no wedding, no span of time, and nothing of the birth itself — only the swift verbs. The child is not named in this verse.

### Scene 2 — The women's words to Naomi (4:14–15)

**3A — Beings**

[[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] — הַנָּשִׁים / "the women"
- Role: the ones who speak to Naomi: blessed be YHWH, who has not left her without a redeemer today
- Relationship: the women who speak to Naomi (4:14)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B3-Naomi]] — נָעֳמִי / Naomi
- Role: the one the women speak to
- Relationship: Ruth's mother-in-law
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B10-YHWH]] — יְהוָה / YHWH
- Role: the one the women bless — who has not left Naomi without a redeemer
- Relationship: the God the women name in their blessing
- Presence: REFERENCED

The child — גֹּאֵל / "a redeemer"
- Role: the newborn; the women say YHWH has not left Naomi without a redeemer today, and that he will be a restorer of her life, for her daughter-in-law has borne him
- Relationship: the son just born
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B9-Ruth]] — כַּלָּתֵךְ אֲשֶׁר־אֲהֵבַתֶךְ / "your daughter-in-law who loves you"
- Role: the one the women praise to Naomi — the bearer, better than seven sons
- Relationship: Ruth; the women do not say her name — she is "your daughter-in-law who loves you"
- Referential form: "your daughter-in-law who loves you … better to you than seven sons"
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL_ISRAEL-Israel]] — בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל / "in Israel"
- Role: where the women wish his name to be called out
- Type: the people and land of Israel
- Effect on scene: the place named in the women's wish

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0008-Blessing]] — בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה / "blessed be YHWH"
- What it is: a blessing in set, weighty form, invoking the divine name
- Function in scene: the women's words to Naomi begin: blessed be YHWH

[[CB_0001-Kinsman-Redeemer]] — גֹּאֵל / "a redeemer"
- What it is: the redeemer — YHWH has not left Naomi without a redeemer today
- Function in scene: the word "redeemer", said at the gate (4:1–8), said again by the women

[[CB_0005-Name-Preservation]] — וְיִקָּרֵא שְׁמוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל / "may his name be called out in Israel"
- What it is: a name called out among the people
- Function in scene: the women's wish: may his name be called out in Israel

[[CB_0046-Seven-Sons-Shibah-Banim]] — טוֹבָה … מִשִּׁבְעָה בָּנִים / "better than seven sons"
- What it is: seven sons — the women's measure
- Function in scene: the women say Ruth is better to Naomi than seven sons

**3D — Times**
- None: no distinct temporal frame; the blessing follows the birth.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] The women say to [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi: blessed be [[B10-YHWH]] YHWH, who has not left you without a redeemer today; may his name be called out in [[PL_ISRAEL-Israel]] Israel. He will be a restorer of your life and a sustainer of your old age — for [[B9-Ruth]] your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
The women speak to Naomi and bless YHWH, who has not left her without a redeemer today; the one born will be a restorer of her life and a sustainer of her old age, and her daughter-in-law, who loves her, is better to her than seven sons.

**Significant Absence**
The women speak to Naomi; they say nothing to Ruth or to Boaz, and Boaz is not mentioned. They do not say Ruth's name or call her the Moabite; she is "your daughter-in-law who loves you".

### Scene 3 — The child on Naomi's lap; the naming (4:16–17)

**3A — Beings**

[[B3-Naomi]] — נָעֳמִי / Naomi
- Role: the one who takes the child to her bosom and becomes his nurse (omenet — the one who looks after a child)
- Relationship: Ruth's mother-in-law; the neighbor-women say a son has been born to her
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] — הַשְּׁכֵנוֹת / "the neighbor-women"
- Role: the ones who call a name for the child, saying a son has been born to Naomi, and call him Obed
- Relationship: the women of the neighborhood
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B25-Obed]] — הַיֶּלֶד / "the child"; עוֹבֵד / Obed
- Role: the child Naomi takes to her bosom; the neighbor-women call him Obed
- Relationship: son of Ruth and Boaz; the neighbor-women say a son has been born to Naomi; the father of Jesse
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B26-Jesse-and-David]] — יִשַׁי … דָּוִד / Jesse … David
- Role: the names the narrator gives after Obed's — Obed's son and grandson
- Relationship: Jesse the son of Obed; David the son of Jesse
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

- None: the text names no place in this scene.

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0047-Obed-Name]] — עוֹבֵד / "Obed"
- What it is: the name the neighbor-women give the child
- Function in scene: the name the neighbor-women call him, after they say a son has been born to Naomi

[[CB_0048-David-Name]] — דָּוִד / "David"
- What it is: the last name in the verse: Jesse is the father of David
- Function in scene: the narrator names David and says nothing more about him

**3D — Times**
- None as the scene's frame: the naming follows the birth; the closing "father of Jesse, father of David" is the narrator's reach to a later time, not a setting within the scene.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B3-Naomi]] Naomi takes the child, sets him on her bosom, and becomes his nurse. [[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] The neighbor-women call out a name for him, saying a son has been born to Naomi; and they call his name [[B25-Obed]] Obed. He is the father of [[B26-Jesse-and-David]] Jesse, the father of David.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Naomi takes the child to her bosom and becomes his nurse; the neighbor-women call a name — a son has been born to Naomi — and call him Obed; and the narrator names Obed's son and grandson, Jesse and David.

**Significant Absence**
Ruth is not mentioned in this scene; the neighbor-women say a son has been born to Naomi. Boaz is not mentioned after 4:13 in this passage. The neighbor-women give the child his name; the text does not say why the name Obed. The narrator names David and says nothing more about him.

## 4. Level 3 — Proposition Inventory

### Proposition 1 — Ruth 4:13a [Scene 1]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** taking as wife
- **Q:** Who took? **A:** [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz
- **Q:** Whom? **A:** [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth
- **Q:** What did she become? **A:** his wife
- **Q:** What happened next? **A:** he came to her

### Proposition 2 — Ruth 4:13b [Scene 1]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** giving conception
- **Q:** Who gave? **A:** [[B10-YHWH]] YHWH
- **Q:** To whom? **A:** [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth

### Proposition 3 — Ruth 4:13c [Scene 1]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** bearing
- **Q:** Who bore? **A:** [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth
- **Q:** What did she bear? **A:** a son

### Proposition 4 — Ruth 4:14a [Scene 2]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** blessing
- **Q:** Who spoke? **A:** [[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] the women
- **Q:** To whom? **A:** [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- **Q:** Whom did they bless? **A:** [[B10-YHWH]] YHWH
- **Q:** What had he not done? **A:** left her without a redeemer today

### Proposition 5 — Ruth 4:14b [Scene 2]
- **Q:** What did they wish? **A:** may his name be called out
- **Q:** Where? **A:** in [[PL_ISRAEL-Israel]] Israel

### Proposition 6 — Ruth 4:15a [Scene 2]
- **Q:** What will the child be? **A:** a restorer of her life
- **Q:** And what else? **A:** a sustainer of her old age

### Proposition 7 — Ruth 4:15b [Scene 2]
- **Q:** Who bore him? **A:** [[B9-Ruth]] her daughter-in-law
- **Q:** What is said of her? **A:** she loves Naomi
- **Q:** How is she measured? **A:** better to Naomi than seven sons

### Proposition 8 — Ruth 4:16a [Scene 3]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** taking the child
- **Q:** Who took him? **A:** [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- **Q:** What did she do? **A:** set him on her bosom

### Proposition 9 — Ruth 4:16b [Scene 3]
- **Q:** What did she become? **A:** his nurse
- **Q:** To whom? **A:** the child

### Proposition 10 — Ruth 4:17a [Scene 3]
- **Q:** What happened? **A:** naming
- **Q:** Who named him? **A:** [[B24-Women-of-Bethlehem]] the neighbor-women
- **Q:** What did they say? **A:** a son has been born to Naomi

### Proposition 11 — Ruth 4:17b [Scene 3]
- **Q:** What name did they call? **A:** [[B25-Obed]] Obed

### Proposition 12 — Ruth 4:17c [Scene 3]
- **Q:** Whose father is he? **A:** [[B26-Jesse-and-David]] Jesse's
- **Q:** And whose father is Jesse? **A:** David's
